facts.fact: The StackAdapt blog advises that marketers often pause programmatic campaigns too early, sometimes after only one day.
facts.quote: This can lead to pausing a campaign too early—sometimes after only one day—if the expected or anticipated results are not immediately realized.

facts.fact: StackAdapt's guidance is that in most cases a programmatic campaign should be checked on the third day after launch.
facts.quote: In most cases, check on your campaign on the third day after launching.

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that results after the first day of a programmatic campaign are not a true indicator of long-term performance.
facts.quote: After the first day, your results will not be a true indicator of long-term performance.

facts.fact: StackAdapt recommends allowing two to three days for a campaign optimization to take effect before making another tweak.
facts.quote: Make an adjustment and allow two to three days for it to take effect before you tweak something else.

facts.fact: As an example, StackAdapt suggests removing a supply source on a Monday and checking campaign performance again on Wednesday, giving the campaign an undisturbed day.
facts.quote: if you remove a supply source on a Monday, give your campaign a full undisturbed day to run and check back on Wednesday.
